title: Why no one can stay without acting

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन । तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: O Janardana, if you consider understanding superior to action, then why do you urge me to this terrible action, O Keshava? Your mixed words confuse my mind; tell me one clear thing by which I may attain what is good.
verses.angle: Arjuna asks why action is urged if wisdom is superior
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Krishna has praised steady wisdom, yet he still asks you to fight. Listen to how Arjuna points out the clash and asks for one clear path.

body.text: Arjuna says: O Janardana, if you consider understanding superior to action, then why do you urge me to this terrible action, O Keshava? Your mixed words confuse my mind; tell me one clear thing by which I may attain what is good. Arjuna hears two different pulls, wisdom praised and battle commanded, and he calls them mixed words that confuse him. He asks for one clear statement that leads to the highest good. Arjuna insists on one clear instruction to cut through the confusion and find his path.

verses.sa: व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे । तदेकं वद निश्िचत्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: Your words seem mixed and confusing to me. Tell me one thing clearly, so I may find the highest good.
verses.angle: evam: the word that shifts blame to the mind
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has already collapsed in despair. Now he pushes Krishna with a direct demand: tell me one clear path that leads to the highest good.

body.text: Arjuna says: Your words seem mixed and confusing to me. Tell me one thing clearly, so I may find the highest good. Arjuna says your words confuse my understanding not by their nature, but because my own mind is entangled. He asks for one teaching not as a student, but as a man demanding a single way out. Krishna answers by telling Arjuna that he has already taught two paths, the path of knowledge and the path of action.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचलोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ । ज्ञानयोगेन सांख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम् ॥
verses.tr: The divine says: In this world, I have already taught two kinds of steadfast practice: the path of knowledge for the contemplative, and the path of action for the active.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna begins his reply by telling Arjuna that human beings differ in make-up, and that two valid paths already exist.

body.text: The divine says: In this world, I have already taught two kinds of steadfast practice: the path of knowledge for the contemplative, and the path of action for the active. Krishna names two temperaments, the contemplative knowers and the active yogis, and assigns each its own path, knowledge and action, before the teaching has even begun. He then warns that simply avoiding action does not lead to freedom.

verses.sa: न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते । न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥
verses.tr: A person does not reach actionless freedom by avoiding action, nor by renouncing action alone does one reach perfection.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is correcting a false choice. Listen for the word san-nyasanat, renunciation, and hear why simply giving things up is not the answer.

body.text: A person does not reach actionless freedom by avoiding action, nor by renouncing action alone does one reach perfection. Avoiding action does not bring freedom, Krishna says, and renouncing alone does not bring the highest state. Krishna then explains that no one can stay still even for a moment, because nature itself drives everyone to act.

verses.sa: न हि कश्िचत्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् । कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥
verses.tr: No one can remain without action even for a moment. Everyone is driven to act by the qualities born of nature.
verses.angle: Avashah: no one is free from action
verses.speaker: Krishna

body.text: No one can remain without action even for a moment. Everyone is driven to act by the qualities born of nature. Notice the word avashah, helpless. No one is in charge of their own stillness. Even when a person sits perfectly still, the qualities of nature move them from the inside. Krishna then moves from the impossibility of inaction to the danger of pretending to act while only thinking of results.

verses.sa: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् । इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥
verses.tr: One who restrains the organs of action but keeps thinking of sense objects in the mind is deluded and called a hypocrite.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna rejects the idea that stopping your hands is enough. Listen to the word he uses for the person who pretends.

body.text: One who restrains the organs of action but keeps thinking of sense objects in the mind is deluded and called a hypocrite. Krishna calls such a person a mithyachari, a false actor, because he restrains his organs of action but keeps his mind feasting on sense objects. Krishna then points to the true path, where a person truly restrains the senses and begins action without attachment.

verses.sa: यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन । कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna, the one who restrains the senses with the mind and begins karma yoga without attachment is श्रेष्ठ.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: How does a person act in the world without drowning in desire? Listen to Krishna's answer about where true control begins.

body.text: Arjuna, the one who restrains the senses with the mind and begins karma yoga without attachment is श्रेष्ठ. Krishna praises the one who reins in the senses with the mind and works without attachment. Krishna then states that even the body cannot be kept alive by pure inaction, so action is unavoidable.

verses.sa: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
verses.tr: Do the duty prescribed for you. Action is better than inaction, and even your body cannot be sustained by inaction.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna turns the argument from fear into motion. Listen for the practical reason he gives for why action is unavoidable.

body.text: Do the duty prescribed for you. Action is better than inaction, and even your body cannot be sustained by inaction. Listen to the word akarma, inaction. Krishna says that even keeping the body alive is not possible through inaction, turning the argument from ethics into biology. He then explains that the only difference is whether actions are done for sacrifice or for personal gain.

verses.sa: यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः । तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसंगः समाचर ॥
verses.tr: Actions done for sacrifice free a person; actions done for personal gain bind. Therefore, Arjuna, do your duty without attachment for that purpose alone.
verses.angle: Karmabandhanah: the world is bound by action
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to the motive behind your work. Listen closely to the word that names the trap we fall into.

body.text: Actions done for sacrifice free a person; actions done for personal gain bind. Therefore, Arjuna, do your duty without attachment for that purpose alone. The word karmabandhanah means bound by action. The world is bound by action not because we work, but because we work for ourselves. Krishna then explains that this was the original law, set at the beginning of time by Prajapati.

verses.sa: सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः । अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक् ॥
verses.tr: In the beginning, Prajapati created beings together with sacrifice and said: “By this, you shall prosper. May this sacrifice be the wish-fulfilling cow for you.”
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna moves Arjuna’s mind from the present battlefield to the very beginning of creation. Hear how the creator first ordered beings to prosper.

body.text: In the beginning, Prajapati created beings together with sacrifice and said: “By this, you shall prosper. May this sacrifice be the wish-fulfilling cow for you.” Krishna names the speaker here as Prajapati, the lord of creatures. By recalling the creator, he shows that sacrifice and duty are not new rules but the original design of life itself. Krishna then explains that by nourishing others through this duty, they in turn nourish you.
